native_xml_definitions.name: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant

scientific_boundary.native_heat_function: Heat energy for chemical-process steam per MJ; water input excluded under the documented closed-loop boundary.
scientific_boundary.source_water_retained: Retain all make-up-water provider quantities plus both direct Water releases with exact compartments and units. This is not a fresh one-kg steam inventory.
scientific_boundary.energy_supply_mix: Complete native chemical-plant heat supply is an explicit same-function/MJ geographic and vintage screening proxy; source fuel and electricity shares are not reconstructed.

reverse.reason: No inverse is inferred. Native MJ chemical heat excludes water. Native kg steam has a separate existing reverse correspondence; inspect its water/feed boundary independently before claiming equivalence.

limitations: Reviewed chemical-plant heat service per MJ, with retained source make-up water and physical water releases. The native original XML explicitly defines one MJ of heat for chemical-process steam and excludes its water input because steam is often used in closed systems. Use that complete positive-reference MJ heat service once, then retain every inspected source tap-water coefficient and both direct water releases separately. Do not use the kg-based fresh-steam process, the old rounded 0.36 kg/MJ factor, or 1 MJ per kg. The two exact markets have only one local unit share of the inspected energy producer; flatten that unit share without adding a second heat service. The target approximates the source regional fuel and electricity mix, combustion efficiencies, technology, vintage, allocation and infrastructure; their LCIA equivalence is not established. Water uses complete native water supply as a geography/vintage proxy, preserving each source provider share separately without normalization. Do not add the original source fuel/electricity inputs to the complete native heat service or count water twice. Canonical water identity, receiving compartment, unit and signed amount remain exact; unsupported native physical water definitions must remain unresolved, never omitted. Factor +1 preserves caller signed MJ, supported uncertainty, formulas, metadata, foreground suppliers and separately listed emissions. Internal source uncertainty/formulas are not reconstructed. Only the 36 enumerated cut-off source profiles are reviewed. Physical kg-steam, allocated chemical co-product steam, individual steam transport, consequential inventories and missing profiles cannot inherit this review. The reverse native heat service has a different water boundary and remains unsupported until separately reviewed; no inverse or water cancellation is inferred.
